[[233 BBY]]–[[232 BBY]]{{YJADate|1}} }} {{Quote|When developing ''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'', the first ''Star Wars'' series created for preschoolers, the creative team never stopped thinking about how this show may be a youngling's first step into a ''larger world'', and their first time experiencing the limitless potential of the ''Star Wars'' galaxy. The show's characters, tone, and the life lessons woven throughout each episode were written just for them, and our talented team was committed to honoring the cinematic legacy while staying true to the expectations of parents for the youngest of audiences.|[[James Waugh]]|}} '''''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures''''' is an animated ''[[Star Wars]]'' series focused for preschoolers, grade schoolers, and their families. It is set during the [[High Republic Era]]. It released on [[Wikipedia:YouTube|YouTube]] with shorts on [[March 27]], [[2023]] and released on [[Disney Junior]], Disney+, Disney Channel, and Disney XD on [[May 4]], 2023. The [[Young Jedi Adventures Season One|first season]] was released in three further batches on [[August 2]], [[November 8]], 2023 and [[February 14]], [[2024]].{{SW|url=news/star-wars-young-jedi-adventures-new-episodes-august-2023|text=Explore New ''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Episodes This Summer}}{{SW|url=news/star-wars-young-jedi-adventures-new-episodes|text=New ''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Episodes Coming Soon}} In 2024, the series was renewed for a [[Young Jedi Adventures Season Two|second season]], with shorts on August 2, the first half released on [[August 14]],{{SW|url=news/young-jedi-adventures-season-2-and-nubs-shorts|text=''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Returns for Season 2}} and the second half on [[March 19]], [[2025]].{{SW|url=news/young-jedi-adventures-season-2-and-nubs-shorts|text=''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Returns for Season 2}} In 2025, the series was renewed for a [[Young Jedi Adventures Season Three|third season]], which released all seven episodes on [[December 8]], 2025. ==Official description== ''Set during The High Republic era, the animated series follows Jedi younglings as they study the ways of the Force, explore the galaxy, help citizens and creatures in need, and learn valuable skills needed to become Jedi along the way.''{{DisneyPlus|subdomain=press|url=news/next-on-disney-plus-april-2023|text=Next on Disney+: April 2023}} ==Development== The show was pitched to [[Lucasfilm]] by [[Michael Olson]] with development beginning in [[2019]].{{InsiderCite|224|The Young Jedi}} On [[May 27]], [[2022]], during [[Celebration Anaheim (2022)|Celebration Anaheim]], the series was announced. It was set during the High Republic era and would focus on a group of Jedi younglings training to be [[Jedi Knight]]s. ''Young Jedi Adventures'' would be the first animated Star Wars series aimed at preschoolers, early grade schoolers, and their families. On [[February 9]], [[2023]], [[Jamaal Avery Jr.]], [[Juliet Donenfeld]], [[Dee Bradley Baker]], [[Emma Berman]], [[Jonathan Lipow]], and [[Piotr Michael]] were confirmed as key cast members. [[StarWars.com]] also announced that the series would premiere on [[May 4]], 2023. ===Production=== {{Quote|I'm going for something a little more specific because this is for children. So, it's got to be clear what's being said. It's almost like with a pre-lingual child or even a dog, where there's a specific intent with the whining or vocalization. If you're a parent, you can often read what that is. And that's kind of what you want with a character like Nubs.|Dee Bradley Baker describing how he voiced his character Nubs|}} [[File:YounglingYJA-BetsyBauer.jpg|300px|thumb|left|Younglings design exploration by [[Betsy Bauer]]]] ''Young Jedi Adventures'' was produced by Lucasfilm in collaboration with [[Wild Canary]], as well as [[ICON Creative Studio]] for Disney+, Disney Junior, and Disney Channel. The series' executive producers included [[James Waugh]], [[Jacqui Lopez]], and [[Josh Rimes]]. The show runner was Michael Olson, who also served as executive producer. [[Elliot M. Bour]] served as co-producer and supervising director. Other producers included [[Jeannine Hodson]] and [[Lamont Magee]]. The animated series was initially produced under the name "Big Wheel." Lucasfilm continued their collaboration with Wild Canary to produce the series' [[Young Jedi Adventures Season Two|second season]]. Waugh, Lopez and Rimes continued as executive producers while Olson continued as show runner and executive producer. Bour continued as supervising director and co-executive producer. [[Lamont Magee]] joined as consulting producer while Icon Creative provided production services for the series. Actors recorded their lines for the series' episodes remotely, with screenwriters and directors stitching the disparate voice performances together. During an interview with [[StarWars.com]], [[Dee Bradley Baker]] likened his character Nubs, who doesn't speak [[Galactic Basic Standard]] (English), to a pre-lingual child or even a dog. Baker recorded multiple options for his characters' lines. Nubs' friends Kai Brightstar and Lys Solay also reinforced what their friend was saying during dialogues, with Baker likening their relationship to that between [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]]. Due to the show's pre-school target audience, sub-titles for Nubs was ruled out by the showrunners.{{SW|url=news/dee-bradley-baker-nubs-interview|text=Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures' Dee Bradley Baker on Creating a Voice for Nubs}} ===Promotion=== A promotional image depicting several characters including [[Yoda]], [[Kai Brightstar]], and [[Nash Durango]] was unveiled at the D23 Expo 2022 on [[September 10]], 2022.{{ThisWeek|IeHXbDSPlPo|All the D23 Expo News, a First Look at Phase II of The High Republic, and More!|sw_url=video/all-the-d23-expo-news-a-first-look-at-phase-ii-of-the-high-republic-and-more}} The series' first official trailer was released at [[Celebration Europe (2023)|Celebration Europe]] on [[April 10]], 2023.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-young-jedi-adventures-trailer|text=Watch the New ''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Trailer}} On [[May 18]], 2023, ''[[This Week! in Star Wars]]'' host [[Kristin Baver]] interviewed cast members [[Jamaal Avery Jr.]] and [[Juliet Donenfeld]], who voiced [[Kai Brightstar]] and [[Lys Solay]] respectively.{{ThisWeek|wAl8b9WZExM|Rise of the Red Blade Reveal, The Mandalorian: The Manga First Look, and More!|sw_url=video/rise-of-the-red-blade-reveal-the-mandalorian-the-manga-first-look-and-more}} On [[July 13]], Baver interviewed [[Emma Berman]] and [[Trey Murphy]], who voiced [[Nash Durango]] and [[Cyrus Vuundir|Taborr Val Dorn]], respectively. The video also announced the release of six further new episodes commencing [[August 2]], 2023.{{ThisWeek|aYGTZacheog|A Look at Ahsoka, More Young Jedi Adventures Episodes, and More!|sw_url=video/a-look-at-ahsoka-more-young-jedi-adventures-episodes-and-more}} ==Release and reception== ===Season One=== Three promotional shorts were released on YouTube on [[March 27]], 2023. Three additional shorts were released over the following weeks leading up to [[April 26]], 2023. These six shorts were subsequently released on Disney+ on April 26.{{DisneyPlus|subdomain=press|url=news/disney-plus-disney-junior-lucasfilm-release-star-wars-young-jedi-adventures-sneak-peek-and-key-art|text=Disney+, Disney Junior, And Lucasfilm Release Sneak Peek Animated Shorts And Key Art For "Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures"}} On [[April 8]], 2023, the first two episodes of the series were screened at the ''Young Jedi Adventures'' panel at Celebration Europe.{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-panel-schedule|text=Plan Ahead with the ''Star Wars'' Celebration Europe 2023 Panel Schedule}} The first seven episodes were released on Disney+ on May 4, 2023.{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-may-2023|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in May 2023}} The seven episodes were also released on a weekly basis on Disney Junior between May 4 and [[June 9]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/showatch/star-wars-young-jedi-adventures/listings|text=Shows A-Z - Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures on Disney Plus|work=[http://www.thefutoncritic.com The Futon Critic]|archiveurl=https://archive.md/S5UCV}} On [[July 13]], 2023, Lucasfilm, Disney+ and Disney Junior announced that six more episodes would be released simultaneously on Disney+ and Disney Junior on August 2. On [[August 18]], 2023, [[StarWars.com]] announced that a third batch of episodes would be released on Disney+ and Disney Junior on [[November 8]], including a [[Life Day]] special set on the [[Wookiee]] homeworld of [[Kashyyyk]]. In addition, further Season One episodes are scheduled to be released in [[2024]]. On [[January 11]], 2024, StarWars.com announced that a fourth batch of episodes would be released on Disney+ and Disney Junior on [[February 14]]. These upcoming episodes included a wilderness training exercise on [[Tenoo]], trips to both [[Black Spire Outpost]] on [[Batuu]] and [[Starlight Beacon]], and a climatic showdown with the antagonistic Taborr Val Dorn. [[Marcus Scribner]], [[Justine Lee]] and [[Liam O'Brien]] were also confirmed as new cast members, playing [[Bell Zettifar]], [[Lina Soh]] and [[Estala Maru]] respectively. [[JeCobi Swain]] was also confirmed as voicing [[Kai Brightstar]] alongside [[Jamaal Avery Jr.]] This brought the total number of episodes in the first season to 25. On [[December 16]], 2023, ''Young Jedi Adventures'' won two [[Wikipedia:Emmy Awards|Emmy Awards]] for "Outstanding Editing for a Preschool Animated Program" and "Outstanding Sound Mixing and Sound Editing for a Preschool Animated Program." The series was also nominated for three other Emmy awards including "Outstanding Pre–School Animated Series," "Outstanding Music Direction and Composition for an Animated Program," and "Outstanding Main Title."{{SW|url=news/star-wars-young-jedi-adventures-emmy-wins-2023|text=''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Wins 2 Children's & Family Emmys}} ===Season Two=== On [[June 14]], 2024, StarWars.com announced that the first half of the [[Young Jedi Adventures Season Two|second season]] would be released on Disney+ and Disney Junior on [[August 14]], with shorts on [[August 2]]. The second half is expected to be released in [[2025]]. A tie-in a digital series called ''[[Star Wars: Fun with Nubs]]'' was also released on June 14. Jedi [[Padawan]] [[Wes Vinik]] portrayed by [[Gunnar Sizemore]] and the [[astromech droid]] [[R0-M1]] were announced as new characters. On [[January 31]], 2025, StarWars.com announced that the second half of the second season would be released on Disney+ and Disney Junior on [[March 19]]. These upcoming episodes would have storylines involving the Jedi younglings joining forces with Prince [[Cyrus Vuundir]] to defend his homeworld from pirates, the younglings and [[Nash Durango]] teaming up to save Master [[Yoda]], and an adult [[Pooba]] named [[Zeepohz|Zeephoz]]. In addition, further episodes of ''Fun with Nubs'' were released in February and March 2025.{{SW|url=news/young-jedi-adventures-season-2-and-nubs-shorts|text=''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Returns for Season 2}} On [[November 18]], [[2025]], the series was nominated for four Emmy Awards: "Outstanding Voice Performer in a Preschool Program" ([[Dee Bradley Baker]], "Outstanding Directing for a Preschool Animated Series" ("[[The Battle of Tenoo]]"), "Outstanding Editing for a Preschool Animated Series" ("The Battle of Tenoo") and "Outstanding Sound Mixing and Sound Editing for a Preschool Animated Program" ("The Battle of Tenoo").{{DisneyCompany|url=children-family-emmy-award-nominations/|text=The Walt Disney Company Dominates Across All Studios and Companies with Record-Breaking 103 Children’s & Family Emmy® Award Nominations|archivedate=20251124024203}}{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsnewsnet.com/2025/11/star-wars-skeleton-crew-young-jedi-adventures-and-rebuild-the-galaxy-all-recognized-in-the-children-family-emmy-nominations.html|text=‘Star Wars: Skeleton Crew,’ ‘Young Jedi Adventures,’ and ‘Rebuild the Galaxy’ All Recognized in the ‘Children & Family Emmy’ Nominations|author=Jay Goodearl|date=2025-11-19|work=Star Wars News Net|archivedate=20251124024633}} ===Season Three=== A [[Young Jedi Adventures Season Three|third season]] was announced at [[Celebration Japan (2025)|Celebration Japan]],{{SW|url=news/star-wars-celebration-2025-young-jedi-adventures-season-3|text=''Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures'' Season 3 Coming This Fall!}} which released on December 8, 2025. The droids [[Beepers]], [[Dozer]], [[Gigi (droid)|Gigi]], [[Dotti]] and the droid builder and tinkerer [[Rek Minuu]] were introduced as new characters. Nubs also appeared at the Kids Corner during Celebration Japan.
